records.literal_gloss: And will become Babylon heaps, a haunt of jackals, a horror and a hissing, without inhabitant.

en.L: And Babylon will become heaps, a haunt of jackals, a horror and a hissing, without inhabitant.
en.B: Babylon will become a heap of ruins, a haunt of jackals, a horror and an object of scorn, where no one lives.
en.R: Babylon will become a pile of ruins where jackals live, a horror and something people mock, a place where no one lives.

es.L: Y Babilonia se convertirá en montones [de ruinas], en guarida de chacales, en horror y en burla, sin habitante.
es.B: Babilonia se convertirá en un montón de ruinas, en guarida de chacales, en un horror y en objeto de burla, donde nadie vive.
es.R: Babilonia se convertirá en un montón de ruinas donde viven los chacales, un horror y algo de lo que la gente se burla, un lugar donde nadie vive.

fr.L: Et Babylone deviendra des monceaux [de pierres], un repaire de chacals, une horreur et un objet de sifflements, sans habitant.
fr.B: Babylone deviendra un amas de ruines, un repaire de chacals, un objet d’horreur et de moquerie, où personne n’habite.
fr.R: Babylone deviendra un tas de ruines où vivent les chacals, un objet d’horreur et de moquerie, un lieu où personne n’habite.

sw.L: Na Babeli itakuwa marundo, makao ya mbweha, kitisho na [kitu cha] kuzomewa, bila mkaaji.
sw.B: Babeli itakuwa rundo la magofu, makao ya mbweha, kitisho na kitu cha kudharauliwa, mahali pasipo na mtu anayeishi.
sw.R: Babeli itakuwa rundo la magofu ambamo mbweha wanaishi, kitisho na kitu ambacho watu hukidhihaki, mahali pasipo na mtu.

decisions.choice: heaps, a haunt of jackals: a city turned to rubble where wild animals live
decisions.reason: As in 9:10 and 10:22, which say the same of Jerusalem: "heaps" are piles of stones from fallen buildings, and jackals make their dens in ruins far from people (49:33; Isaiah 13:22). What Babylon did to Jerusalem is done to Babylon.

decisions.choice: a horror and a hissing: a ruin that makes passers-by gasp and whistle
decisions.reason: As in 18:16 and 25:9: people who passed a destroyed place were appalled and whistled in shock and scorn (50:13).

decisions.choice: horror, hissing / horror, object of scorn / horror, something people mock
decisions.reason: The wording settled for this pair in Jeremiah. The Hebrew verse is a single line; Literal and Balanced divide it once because it is long, and Readable keeps it as one line.

decisions.choice: horror y burla (L); un horror y objeto de burla (B); un horror y algo de lo que la gente se burla (R)
decisions.reason: The list wording set for Jeremiah (horror, hissing).

decisions.choice: "kitisho na [kitu cha] kuzomewa" (L); "kitisho na kitu cha kudharauliwa" (B); "kitisho na kitu ambacho watu hukidhihaki" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for the lists of horror and hissing in Swahili Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: "une horreur et un objet de sifflements" (L); "un objet d’horreur et de moquerie" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The horror-and-hissing pair in the same French throughout Jeremiah (18:16; 19:8; 25:9, 18).

source.text: יַחְדָּ֖ו כַּכְּפִרִ֣ים יִשְׁאָ֑גוּ נָעֲר֖וּ כְּגוֹרֵ֥י אֲרָיֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Together like young lions they roar; they growl like cubs of lions.

en.L: Together they roar like young lions; \q they growl like lions' cubs.
en.B: They roar together like young lions; \q they growl like lion cubs.
en.R: The people of Babylon roar together like young lions. \q They growl like hungry lion cubs.

es.L: Juntos rugen como leoncillos; \q gruñen como cachorros de leones.
es.B: Rugen juntos como leones jóvenes; \q gruñen como cachorros de león.
es.R: La gente de Babilonia ruge junta como leones jóvenes. \q Gruñen como cachorros de león hambrientos.

fr.L: Ensemble ils rugissent comme des lionceaux ; \q ils grondent comme des petits de lionnes.
fr.B: Ils rugissent ensemble comme de jeunes lions ; \q ils grognent comme des lionceaux.
fr.R: Les habitants de Babylone rugissent tous ensemble comme de jeunes lions. \q Ils grognent comme des lionceaux affamés.

sw.L: Pamoja wananguruma kama wana-simba; \q wanakoroma kama watoto wa simba.
sw.B: Wananguruma pamoja kama wana-simba; \q wanakoroma kama watoto wa simba.
sw.R: Watu wa Babeli wananguruma pamoja kama wana-simba. \q Wanakoroma kama watoto wa simba wenye njaa.

decisions.choice: they roar ... they growl: the Babylonians, greedy for prey
decisions.reason: The verse most likely describes the Babylonians themselves: like lions roaring over their kill, they are eager to devour (compare 2:15; 50:17). Verse 39 turns their hunger into a feast that ends in death. Some read the lions as the attackers, but "them" in verse 39 points back to these lions as the ones made drunk.

decisions.choice: The people of Babylon; hungry
decisions.reason: Readable names who roars (m1) and adds "hungry" to explain why lions roar and growl here.

source.text: בְּחֻמָּ֞ם אָשִׁ֣ית אֶת־מִשְׁתֵּיהֶ֗ם וְהִשְׁכַּרְתִּים֙ לְמַ֣עַן יַעֲלֹ֔זוּ וְיָשְׁנ֥וּ שְׁנַת־עוֹלָ֖ם וְלֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: In their being heated I will set their feast and I will make them drunk so that they exult, and they will sleep a sleep of forever and not wake, declares Yahweh.

en.L: When they are heated, I will set out their feast \q and make them drunk, so that they exult, \q and they will sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: While they are heated with greed, I will set out a feast for them \q and make them drunk, so that they shout and laugh, \q and they will sleep a sleep that lasts forever and never wake, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: While they are hot with hunger, I will set out a feast for them. \q I will make them drunk, and they will celebrate. \q Then they will fall asleep forever and never wake up, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Cuando estén enardecidos, les pondré su banquete \q y los embriagaré, para que se alegren, \q y duerman un sueño perpetuo y no despierten, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Mientras estén enardecidos por la codicia, les prepararé un banquete \q y los emborracharé, para que griten y rían, \q y duerman un sueño que dure para siempre y nunca despierten, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Mientras estén ardiendo de hambre, les prepararé un banquete. \q Los emborracharé, y ellos harán fiesta. \q Luego se dormirán para siempre y nunca despertarán, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Quand ils seront échauffés, je leur servirai leur festin \q et je les enivrerai, pour qu’ils exultent, \q et ils dormiront d’un sommeil éternel et ne se réveilleront pas, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Pendant qu’ils brûlent d’avidité, je leur préparerai un festin \q et je les enivrerai, pour qu’ils crient et rient ; \q puis ils dormiront d’un sommeil sans fin et ne se réveilleront jamais, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Pendant qu’ils brûlent d’appétit, je leur préparerai un festin. \q Je les enivrerai, et ils feront la fête. \q Puis ils s’endormiront pour toujours et ne se réveilleront jamais, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Watakapokuwa na joto, nitaandaa karamu yao \q na kuwalevya, ili washangilie, \q nao watalala usingizi wa milele wasiamke, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Wakiwa wamechemka kwa tamaa, nitawaandalia karamu \q na kuwalevya, ili wapige kelele na kucheka, \q nao watalala usingizi wa milele wasiamke kamwe, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Wakiwa na njaa kali, nitawaandalia karamu. \q Nitawalevya, nao watasherehekea. \q Kisha watalala usingizi milele wala hawataamka kamwe, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: when they are heated: in the heat of their greed or of their drinking
decisions.reason: The verb means to grow hot. It may mean the heat of the lions' hunger (verse 38) or the flush of wine at a feast (Hosea 7:5-7).

decisions.choice: I will set out their feast and make them drunk: the cup of judgment as a deadly banquet
decisions.reason: The LORD himself prepares the feast. Babylon, who made the nations drunk (verse 7), now drinks the cup of his wrath (25:15-16, 27). The story of Babylon's fall during a royal banquet (Daniel 5:1-4, 30) fits the picture.

decisions.choice: sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake: die
decisions.reason: Sleep from which there is no waking is death (Psalm 13:4; Job 14:12). The same words return in verse 57.

decisions.choice: so that they exult: the Greek reads "so that they are stunned"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says they will exult, the noisy joy of drinkers, just before they fall into the sleep of death. The Greek translation reads "so that they may be stupefied", which may reflect a Hebrew verb of similar letters meaning "faint" (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: a sleep that lasts forever and never wake (B); fall asleep forever and never wake up (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording is used at each level in verse 57. Balanced adds "with greed" to show what the heat is (m1); Readable says "hunger".

source.text: אֽוֹרִידֵ֖ם כְּכָרִ֣ים לִטְב֑וֹחַ כְּאֵילִ֖ים עִם־עַתּוּדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: I will bring them down like lambs to slaughter, like rams with male goats.

en.L: I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, \q like rams together with male goats.
en.B: I will lead them down like lambs to be slaughtered, \q like rams and male goats.
en.R: I will lead them away like lambs to be killed, \q like rams and goats.

es.L: Los haré descender como corderos al matadero, \q como carneros junto con machos cabríos.
es.B: Los llevaré como corderos al matadero, \q como carneros y machos cabríos.
es.R: Los llevaré como corderos para que los maten, \q como carneros y chivos.

fr.L: Je les ferai descendre comme des agneaux à l’abattoir, \q comme des béliers avec des boucs.
fr.B: Je les ferai descendre comme des agneaux qu’on va égorger, \q comme des béliers et des boucs.
fr.R: Je les emmènerai comme des agneaux qu’on va tuer, \q comme des béliers et des boucs.

sw.L: Nitawashusha kama wana-kondoo machinjoni, \q kama kondoo dume pamoja na mabeberu.
sw.B: Nitawaongoza kushuka kama wana-kondoo wanaopelekwa kuchinjwa, \q kama kondoo dume na mabeberu.
sw.R: Nitawapeleka kama wana-kondoo wanaopelekwa kuuawa, \q kama kondoo dume na mbuzi.

decisions.choice: lambs, rams, male goats: animals led to sacrifice
decisions.reason: The animals are those offered in sacrifice (Isaiah 34:6; Ezekiel 39:18). Babylon's people, the lions of verse 38, are now led down like tame sheep to be killed (11:19; 50:27).

source.text: אֵ֚יךְ נִלְכְּדָ֣ה שֵׁשַׁ֔ךְ וַתִּתָּפֵ֖שׂ תְּהִלַּ֣ת כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ אֵ֣יךְ הָיְתָ֧ה לְשַׁמָּ֛ה בָּבֶ֖ל בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: How has been captured Sheshach, and has been seized [the] praise of all the earth! How has become a horror Babylon among the nations!

en.L: How Sheshach has been captured, \q and the praise of all the earth seized! \q How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
en.B: How Sheshach is taken, \q the pride of the whole earth seized! \q How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
en.R: Sheshach, that is, Babylon, has been captured! \q The city that the whole world praised has been taken! \q Babylon has become a horror among the nations!

es.L: ¡Cómo ha sido tomada Sesac, \q y apresada la alabanza de toda la tierra! \q ¡Cómo se ha convertido Babilonia en objeto de horror entre las naciones!
es.B: ¡Cómo ha caído Sesac, \q tomada la gloria de toda la tierra! \q ¡Cómo se ha convertido Babilonia en un horror entre las naciones!
es.R: ¡Sesac, es decir, Babilonia, ha sido conquistada! \q ¡La ciudad que todo el mundo alababa ha sido tomada! \q ¡Babilonia se ha convertido en un horror entre las naciones!

fr.L: Comme Shéshak a été prise, \q et la gloire de toute la terre saisie ! \q Comme Babylone est devenue un objet d’horreur parmi les nations !
fr.B: Comme Shéshak est prise, \q la fierté de toute la terre saisie ! \q Comme Babylone est devenue un objet d’horreur parmi les nations !
fr.R: Shéshak, c’est-à-dire Babylone, a été prise ! \q La ville que le monde entier admirait a été prise ! \q Babylone est devenue un objet d’horreur parmi les nations !

sw.L: Jinsi Sheshaki ilivyotwaliwa, \q na sifa ya dunia yote ilivyokamatwa! \q Jinsi Babeli ilivyokuwa kitisho kati ya mataifa!
sw.B: Jinsi Sheshaki ilivyotekwa, \q fahari ya dunia yote ilivyokamatwa! \q Jinsi Babeli ilivyokuwa kitisho kati ya mataifa!
sw.R: Sheshaki, yaani Babeli, imetekwa! \q Mji ambao dunia yote iliusifu umechukuliwa! \q Babeli imekuwa kitisho kati ya mataifa!

decisions.choice: Sheshach: a coded name for Babylon
decisions.reason: As in 25:26, Sheshach is Babylon written in the code called *atbash*. Here it stands in parallel with "Babylon" in the next line, which shows what it means. The Greek translation lacks the name here (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: the praise of all the earth: the city all the world admired
decisions.reason: Babylon was the glory and pride of the nations (Isaiah 13:19). The same words are used of Jerusalem in 49:25 and Zephaniah 3:19.

decisions.choice: How ...!: a cry of astonishment, as in a lament
decisions.reason: The word opens a lament over a fall that seemed impossible (Isaiah 14:4, 12; Lamentations 1:1).

decisions.choice: Sheshach, that is, Babylon; The city that the whole world praised
decisions.reason: As in 25:26, Readable adds what the coded name stands for. It turns the exclamations into plain statements.

decisions.choice: Sesac
decisions.reason: A coded name for Babylon (25:26), made by swapping letters of the alphabet; Readable says what it stands for.

decisions.choice: "Sheshaki" kept as a name; Readable adds "yaani Babeli"
decisions.reason: As the English: Sheshach is a coded name for Babylon, which the meaning decision explains.

source.text: עָלָ֥ה עַל־בָּבֶ֖ל הַיָּ֑ם בַּהֲמ֥וֹן גַּלָּ֖יו נִכְסָֽתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Has gone up over Babylon the sea; with [the] roar of its waves she has been covered.

en.L: The sea has gone up over Babylon; \q she has been covered with the roar of its waves.
en.B: The sea has risen over Babylon; \q she is covered by its roaring waves.
en.R: An army like the sea has risen over Babylon. \q She is covered with its roaring waves.

es.L: Subió el mar sobre Babilonia; \q con el estruendo de sus olas ha sido cubierta.
es.B: El mar ha subido sobre Babilonia; \q la cubren sus olas que rugen.
es.R: Un ejército como el mar ha subido sobre Babilonia. \q La cubren sus olas que rugen.

fr.L: La mer est montée sur Babylone ; \q elle a été couverte par le tumulte de ses vagues.
fr.B: La mer a submergé Babylone ; \q elle est recouverte par ses vagues grondantes.
fr.R: Une armée pareille à la mer a submergé Babylone. \q Elle est recouverte par ses vagues grondantes.

sw.L: Bahari imepanda juu ya Babeli; \q amefunikwa kwa mngurumo wa mawimbi yake.
sw.B: Bahari imepanda juu ya Babeli; \q amefunikwa na mawimbi yake yanayonguruma.
sw.R: Jeshi lililo kama bahari limepanda juu ya Babeli. \q Amefunikwa na mawimbi yake yanayonguruma.

decisions.choice: the sea ... its waves: the invading army as a flood
decisions.reason: A great army is often pictured as a flood (46:7-8; 47:2; Isaiah 8:7-8). Babylon, whose own sea the LORD will dry up (verse 36), is drowned by a greater sea: the nations sent against her.

decisions.choice: An army like the sea
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sea stands for (m1).

source.text: הָי֤וּ עָרֶ֨יהָ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה אֶ֖רֶץ צִיָּ֣ה וַעֲרָבָ֑ה אֶ֗רֶץ לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֤ב בָּהֵן֙ כָּל־אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־יַעֲבֹ֥ר בָּהֵ֖ן בֶּן־אָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Have become her cities a horror, a land of drought and desert, a land not dwells in them any man, and not passes through them a son of man.

en.L: Her cities have become a horror, \q a land of drought and desert, \q a land in which no one dwells, \q and through which no son of man passes.
en.B: Her towns have become a horror, \q a dry land and a desert, \q a land where no one lives, \q where no human being passes through.
en.R: Babylon's towns have become empty ruins. \q The land is dry like a desert. \q No one lives there. \q No one even travels through it.

es.L: Sus ciudades se han convertido en objeto de horror, \q tierra de sequía y de desierto, \q tierra en que no habita nadie \q y por la que no pasa {{gender:ningún ser humano|hijo de hombre}}.
es.B: Sus ciudades se han convertido en un horror, \q una tierra seca y un desierto, \q una tierra donde nadie vive, \q por donde no pasa ningún ser humano.
es.R: Las ciudades de Babilonia se han convertido en ruinas vacías. \q La tierra está seca como un desierto. \q Nadie vive allí. \q Nadie pasa siquiera por allí.

fr.L: Ses villes sont devenues un objet d’horreur, \q une terre de sécheresse et de steppe, \q une terre où personne n’habite \q et par où ne passe aucun fils d’homme.
fr.B: Ses villes sont devenues un objet d’horreur, \q une terre aride et un désert, \q une terre où personne n’habite, \q où ne passe aucun être humain.
fr.R: Les villes de Babylone sont devenues des ruines vides. \q Le pays est sec comme un désert. \q Personne n’y habite. \q Personne ne le traverse même.

sw.L: Miji yake imekuwa kitisho, \q nchi ya ukame na jangwa, \q nchi ambayo hakuna mtu akaaye ndani yake, \q wala mwanadamu hapiti ndani yake.
sw.B: Miji yake imekuwa kitisho, \q nchi kame na jangwa, \q nchi ambayo hakuna mtu anayeishi ndani yake, \q ambayo hakuna mwanadamu anayepita ndani yake.
sw.R: Miji ya Babeli imekuwa magofu matupu. \q Nchi ni kavu kama jangwa. \q Hakuna mtu anayeishi huko. \q Hakuna mtu hata anayepita ndani yake.

decisions.choice: a horror: a ruin that appalls those who see it
decisions.reason: The word means both desolation and the shock it causes (verse 37). Babylon's well-watered land becomes a desert, as Jerusalem's did (2:6; 4:26-27).

decisions.choice: son of man: a human being
decisions.reason: The phrase means any human being (49:18, 33; 50:40). Not even a traveler will pass through.

decisions.choice: towns; human being
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "towns" for the many smaller places, as in 9:10, and "human being" for "son of man" (m2). Readable says "empty ruins" for "horror" here, where the sense is the ruin itself.

source.text: וּפָקַדְתִּ֨י עַל־בֵּ֜ל בְּבָבֶ֗ל וְהֹצֵאתִ֤י אֶת־בִּלְעוֹ֙ מִפִּ֔יו וְלֹֽא־יִנְהֲר֥וּ אֵלָ֛יו ע֖וֹד גּוֹיִ֑ם גַּם־חוֹמַ֥ת בָּבֶ֖ל נָפָֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will punish Bel in Babylon, and I will bring out what he swallowed from his mouth, and not will stream to him again nations; also [the] wall of Babylon has fallen.

en.L: And I will punish Bel in Babylon, and I will bring out of his mouth what he has swallowed, \q and nations will no longer stream to him; \q even the wall of Babylon has fallen.
en.B: I will punish Bel in Babylon and make him spit out what he has swallowed. \q Nations will stream to him no more; \q even Babylon's wall has fallen.
en.R: I will punish Bel, the god of Babylon. I will make him spit out what he swallowed. \q The nations will not come in crowds to worship him any more. \q Even the wall of Babylon has fallen.

es.L: Y castigaré a Bel en Babilonia, y sacaré de su boca lo que se ha tragado, \q y ya no acudirán a él las naciones; \q también el muro de Babilonia ha caído.
es.B: Castigaré a Bel en Babilonia y le haré escupir lo que se tragó. \q Ya no acudirán a él las naciones; \q hasta el muro de Babilonia ha caído.
es.R: Castigaré a Bel, el dios de Babilonia. Le haré escupir lo que se tragó. \q Las naciones ya no vendrán en multitudes a adorarlo. \q Hasta el muro de Babilonia ha caído.

fr.L: Et je punirai Bel à Babylone, et je ferai sortir de sa bouche ce qu’il a englouti, \q et les nations n’afflueront plus vers lui ; \q même la muraille de Babylone est tombée.
fr.B: Je punirai Bel à Babylone et je lui ferai recracher ce qu’il a englouti. \q Les nations n’afflueront plus vers lui ; \q même la muraille de Babylone est tombée.
fr.R: Je punirai Bel, le dieu de Babylone. Je lui ferai recracher ce qu’il a avalé. \q Les nations ne viendront plus en foule pour l’adorer. \q Même la muraille de Babylone est tombée.

sw.L: Nami nitamwadhibu Beli katika Babeli, nami nitatoa kinywani mwake kile alichokimeza, \q wala mataifa hawatamiminikia tena; \q hata ukuta wa Babeli umeanguka.
sw.B: Nitamwadhibu Beli katika Babeli na kumfanya akitapike alichokimeza. \q Mataifa hawatamiminikia tena; \q hata ukuta wa Babeli umeanguka.
sw.R: Nitamwadhibu Beli, mungu wa Babeli. Nitamfanya akitapike alichokimeza. \q Mataifa hayatakuja tena kwa makundi kumwabudu. \q Hata ukuta wa Babeli umeanguka.

decisions.choice: Bel: Marduk, the chief god of Babylon
decisions.reason: Bel means "lord" and was a title of Marduk, Babylon's patron god (50:2; Isaiah 46:1).

decisions.choice: bring out of his mouth what he has swallowed: Babylon must give back what she took
decisions.reason: In verse 34 Zion says that Nebuchadrezzar swallowed her like a sea monster. Now the LORD makes Babylon's god give back what he swallowed: the people and treasures taken from the nations, among them the exiles and the vessels of the temple (27:16-22; 52:17-23; Ezra 1:7-11).

decisions.choice: nations will no longer stream to him: Babylon will no longer draw the peoples
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the nations streaming to Zion (Isaiah 2:2; Jeremiah 31:12). The crowds of worshipers and tribute-bearers who flowed to Bel's city will stop.

decisions.choice: the Greek translation lacks the words from here to the middle of verse 49
decisions.reason: The Greek translation of Jeremiah, which is shorter than the Hebrew throughout (1:1), does not have the text from "nations will no longer stream to him" in this verse to "the slain of Israel" in verse 49 (this is from general knowledge). The Hebrew text is translated here in full.

decisions.choice: the god of Babylon; come in crowds to worship him
decisions.reason: Readable explains who Bel is (m1) and what the streaming of the nations means (m3).

source.text: צְא֤וּ מִתּוֹכָהּ֙ עַמִּ֔י וּמַלְּט֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־נַפְשׁ֑וֹ מֵחֲר֖וֹן אַף־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Go out from her midst, my people, and save each his life from [the] burning anger of Yahweh.

en.L: Go out from her midst, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q and save your lives, each one, from the burning anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Come out of her, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people! \q Every one of you, run for your life from the fierce anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!
en.R: Come out of Babylon, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people! \q Everyone, run for your life to escape {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s terrible anger!

es.L: {{plural_you:Salgan|Salid}} de en medio de ella, pueblo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, \q y {{plural_you:salven|salvad}} cada uno su vida del ardor de la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Salgan|Salid}} de ella, pueblo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}! \q ¡Que cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} corra para salvar su vida de la ira ardiente {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}!
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Salgan|Salid}} de Babilonia, pueblo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}! \q ¡Que todos corran para salvar su vida y escapar de la terrible ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}!

fr.L: Sortez du milieu d’elle, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, \q et sauvez chacun sa vie de la colère ardente {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Sortez de là, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple ! \q Que chacun de vous sauve sa vie devant la colère ardente {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} !
fr.R: Sortez de Babylone, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple ! \q Que chacun sauve sa vie pour échapper à la terrible colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} !

sw.L: Tokeni katikati yake, watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, \q na kila mtu aokoe nafsi yake kutoka katika hasira kali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Tokeni ndani yake, enyi watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}! \q Kila mmoja wenu, kimbieni kuokoa maisha yenu kutoka katika hasira kali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!
sw.R: Tokeni Babeli, enyi watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}! \q Kila mtu, kimbia kuokoa maisha yako, uepuke hasira kali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!

decisions.choice: go out from her midst, my people: the call to the exiles to leave Babylon
decisions.reason: The call of verse 6 returns, now as the LORD's own word to "my people" (50:8; Isaiah 48:20; 52:11). Revelation 18:4 takes it up: "Come out of her, my people".

decisions.choice: the burning anger of the LORD: his fierce anger
decisions.reason: Literally "the burning of the nose of the LORD", a set phrase for his anger at its height (4:8, 26; 25:37-38).

decisions.choice: run for your life
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

source.text: וּפֶן־יֵרַ֤ךְ לְבַבְכֶם֙ וְתִֽירְא֔וּ בַּשְּׁמוּעָ֖ה הַנִּשְׁמַ֣עַת בָּאָ֑רֶץ וּבָ֧א בַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁמוּעָ֗ה וְאַחֲרָ֤יו בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הַשְּׁמוּעָ֔ה וְחָמָ֣ס בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמֹשֵׁ֖ל עַל־מֹשֵֽׁל׃

records.literal_gloss: And lest grow faint your heart and you fear at the report heard in the land, and comes in a year the report and after it in a year the report, and violence in the land, and ruler against ruler.

en.L: And let not your heart grow faint, and do not be afraid \q at the report heard in the land, \q when a report comes in one year, and after it a report in [another] year, \q and violence [is] in the land, and ruler [rises] against ruler.
en.B: Do not lose heart or be afraid \q at the rumors heard in the land, \q one rumor this year, another the next, \q rumors of violence in the land and of ruler against ruler.
en.R: Do not lose courage or be afraid \q when you hear news in the land. \q One year there will be one report, and the next year another. \q There will be violence in the land, and one ruler will fight against another.

es.L: Y que no desmaye {{plural_you:su corazón|vuestro corazón}}, ni {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo \q por el rumor que se oye en la tierra, \q cuando venga un año un rumor, y después otro año otro rumor, \q y [haya] violencia en la tierra, y gobernante contra gobernante.
es.B: No {{plural_you:se desanimen|os desaniméis}} ni {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo \q por los rumores que se oyen en la tierra, \q un rumor este año, otro el siguiente, \q rumores de violencia en la tierra y de gobernante contra gobernante.
es.R: No {{plural_you:pierdan|perdáis}} el valor ni {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo \q cuando {{plural_you:oigan|oigáis}} noticias en la tierra. \q Un año habrá una noticia, y al año siguiente otra. \q Habrá violencia en la tierra, y un gobernante peleará contra otro.

fr.L: Et que votre cœur ne faiblisse pas, et n’ayez pas peur \q de la rumeur entendue dans le pays, \q quand une rumeur vient une année, et après elle une rumeur [une autre] année, \q et que la violence [est] dans le pays, et dominateur contre dominateur.
fr.B: Ne perdez pas courage et n’ayez pas peur \q des rumeurs qu’on entend dans le pays : \q une rumeur cette année, une autre l’année suivante, \q des rumeurs de violence dans le pays et de dirigeant contre dirigeant.
fr.R: Ne perdez pas courage et n’ayez pas peur \q quand vous entendrez des nouvelles dans le pays. \q Une année, on dira une chose, et l’année suivante, une autre. \q Il y aura de la violence dans le pays, et les chefs se battront entre eux.

sw.L: Na moyo wenu usizimie, wala msiogope \q kwa habari itakayosikiwa katika nchi, \q habari ikija mwaka mmoja, na baada yake habari mwaka [mwingine], \q na udhalimu [uko] katika nchi, na mtawala [anainuka] juu ya mtawala.
sw.B: Msife moyo wala msiogope \q kwa uvumi utakaosikiwa katika nchi, \q uvumi mmoja mwaka huu, mwingine mwaka unaofuata, \q uvumi wa udhalimu katika nchi na wa mtawala dhidi ya mtawala.
sw.R: Msipoteze ujasiri wala msiogope \q mnaposikia habari katika nchi. \q Mwaka mmoja itakuwako habari moja, na mwaka unaofuata nyingine. \q Kutakuwa na udhalimu katika nchi, na mtawala mmoja atapigana na mwingine.

decisions.choice: and lest your heart grow faint: do not lose heart
decisions.reason: The verse warns the exiles not to be shaken by the news that comes before Babylon's end. The word "lest" carries on from the call of verse 45: go out, and do not be afraid.

decisions.choice: the report: news or rumors of unrest
decisions.reason: The word means news heard by word of mouth (10:22; 49:14, 23). Year after year rumors come of violence and of rulers fighting each other.

decisions.choice: ruler against ruler: struggles for power in Babylon
decisions.reason: After Nebuchadnezzar died in 562 BC, Babylon had four kings in seven years, two of them killed in plots, before the last king, Nabonidus. The words may refer to such unrest, or to wars between Babylon's rulers and their rivals.

decisions.choice: [another]; [is]; [rises]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words English needs. Balanced and Readable say "rumors" and "news" for the report (m2).

source.text: לָכֵן֙ הִנֵּ֣ה יָמִ֣ים בָּאִ֔ים וּפָקַדְתִּי֙ עַל־פְּסִילֵ֣י בָבֶ֔ל וְכָל־אַרְצָ֖הּ תֵּב֑וֹשׁ וְכָל־חֲלָלֶ֖יהָ יִפְּל֥וּ בְתוֹכָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore here days coming and I will punish [the] idols of Babylon, and all her land will be ashamed, and all her slain will fall in her midst.

en.L: Therefore, look, days are coming \q when I will punish the idols of Babylon; \q her whole land will be put to shame, \q and all her slain will fall in her midst.
en.B: Therefore the days are coming \q when I will punish Babylon's idols. \q Her whole land will be put to shame, \q and all her slain will fall within her.
en.R: So the time is coming \q when I will punish Babylon's idols. \q Her whole land will be ashamed, \q and her people will lie dead everywhere in the city.

es.L: Por tanto, he aquí vienen días \q en que castigaré a los ídolos de Babilonia; \q toda su tierra será avergonzada, \q y todos sus muertos caerán en medio de ella.
es.B: Por eso vienen días \q en que castigaré a los ídolos de Babilonia. \q Toda su tierra será avergonzada, \q y todos sus muertos caerán dentro de ella.
es.R: Por eso se acerca el tiempo \q en que castigaré a los ídolos de Babilonia. \q Toda su tierra quedará avergonzada, \q y su gente quedará muerta por toda la ciudad.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, voici, des jours viennent \q où je punirai les idoles de Babylone ; \q tout son pays sera couvert de honte, \q et tous ses blessés à mort tomberont au milieu d’elle.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi des jours viennent \q où je punirai les idoles de Babylone. \q Tout son pays sera couvert de honte, \q et tous ses morts tomberont au milieu d’elle.
fr.R: C’est pourquoi un temps vient \q où je punirai les idoles de Babylone. \q Tout son pays aura honte, \q et ses habitants seront étendus morts partout dans la ville.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo, tazama, siku zinakuja \q nitakapoziadhibu sanamu za Babeli; \q nchi yake yote itaaibishwa, \q na waliouawa wake wote wataanguka katikati yake.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo siku zinakuja \q nitakapoziadhibu sanamu za Babeli. \q Nchi yake yote itaaibishwa, \q na wote waliouawa wataanguka ndani yake.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo wakati unakuja \q nitakapoziadhibu sanamu za Babeli. \q Nchi yake yote itaona aibu, \q na watu wake watalala wamekufa kila mahali mjini.

decisions.choice: punish the idols: deal with the carved gods of Babylon
decisions.reason: The verb means to visit and settle accounts (verse 18). The idols are the carved images of Babylon's gods (50:2, 38). Verse 52 repeats the line.

decisions.choice: put to shame: disgraced when its gods fail
decisions.reason: Those who trusted in the idols are shamed when the idols cannot save them (verse 17; 10:14).

decisions.choice: look, days are coming (L); the days are coming (B); the time is coming (R)
decisions.reason: The formula keeps the wording used elsewhere in Jeremiah (7:32; 16:14; 23:5).

source.text: וְרִנְּנ֤וּ עַל־בָּבֶל֙ שָׁמַ֣יִם וָאָ֔רֶץ וְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּהֶ֑ם כִּ֧י מִצָּפ֛וֹן יָבוֹא־לָ֥הּ הַשּׁוֹדְדִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will shout for joy over Babylon heaven and earth and all that [is] in them, for from [the] north will come to her the destroyers, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And heaven and earth and all that [is] in them \q will shout for joy over Babylon, \q for from the north the destroyers will come against her, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then heaven and earth and everything in them \q will sing for joy over Babylon, \q for destroyers will come against her from the north, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then the sky and the earth and everything in them \q will shout for joy because of what happens to Babylon. \q Armies will come from the north and destroy her, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y los cielos y la tierra y todo lo que [hay] en ellos \q cantarán de júbilo sobre Babilonia, \q porque del norte vendrán contra ella los destructores, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Entonces los cielos y la tierra y todo lo que hay en ellos \q cantarán de alegría por Babilonia, \q porque los destructores vendrán contra ella desde el norte, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Entonces el cielo y la tierra y todo lo que hay en ellos \q gritarán de alegría por lo que le pase a Babilonia. \q Vendrán ejércitos del norte y la destruirán, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et les cieux et la terre et tout ce qui [est] en eux \q pousseront des cris de joie sur Babylone, \q car du nord les dévastateurs viendront contre elle, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Alors le ciel et la terre et tout ce qu’ils contiennent \q chanteront de joie sur Babylone, \q car des dévastateurs viendront du nord contre elle, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Alors le ciel et la terre et tout ce qu’ils contiennent \q pousseront des cris de joie à cause de ce qui arrivera à Babylone. \q Des armées viendront du nord pour la détruire, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Na mbingu na nchi na vyote [vilivyomo] ndani yake \q vitashangilia juu ya Babeli, \q kwa maana kutoka kaskazini waharibu watamjia, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Ndipo mbingu na nchi na kila kitu kilichomo \q vitaimba kwa furaha juu ya Babeli, \q kwa maana waharibu watamjia kutoka kaskazini, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Ndipo anga na dunia na kila kitu kilichomo \q vitapiga kelele za furaha kwa sababu ya yale yatakayoipata Babeli. \q Majeshi yatakuja kutoka kaskazini na kuiangamiza, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: heaven and earth will shout for joy: all creation rejoices at Babylon's fall
decisions.reason: Heaven and earth are called to rejoice at what God does (Isaiah 44:23; 49:13). Revelation 18:20 takes up the scene: "Rejoice over her, heaven".

decisions.choice: from the north ... the destroyers: the armies from the northern lands
decisions.reason: Judah's destroyer once came "from the north" (1:14; 4:6; 6:1). Now Babylon's destroyers come from the north too: the Medes and the peoples of verse 27 (50:3, 9, 41).

decisions.choice: Armies will come ... and destroy her
decisions.reason: Readable says "armies" for the destroyers, since verses 27-28 have named them.

source.text: גַּם־בָּבֶ֕ל לִנְפֹּ֖ל חַֽלְלֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל גַּם־לְבָבֶ֥ל נָפְל֖וּ חַֽלְלֵ֥י כָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Also Babylon [is] to fall, [O] slain of Israel, as also for Babylon have fallen [the] slain of all the earth.

en.L: Babylon too must fall, \q for the slain of Israel, \q just as for Babylon the slain of all the earth have fallen.
en.B: Babylon must fall \q because of Israel's slain, \q just as because of Babylon the slain of the whole earth have fallen.
en.R: Babylon killed people all over the world. \q She killed the people of Israel too. \q Now Babylon herself must fall.

es.L: También Babilonia ha de caer \q por los muertos de Israel, \q así como por Babilonia han caído los muertos de toda la tierra.
es.B: Babilonia tiene que caer \q por causa de los muertos de Israel, \q así como por causa de Babilonia han caído los muertos de toda la tierra.
es.R: Babilonia mató a gente de todo el mundo. \q También mató a gente de Israel. \q Ahora le toca caer a Babilonia.

fr.L: Babylone aussi doit tomber, \q pour les blessés à mort d’Israël, \q comme pour Babylone sont tombés les blessés à mort de toute la terre.
fr.B: Babylone doit tomber \q à cause des morts d’Israël, \q comme à cause de Babylone sont tombés les morts de toute la terre.
fr.R: Babylone a tué des gens dans le monde entier. \q Elle a tué aussi le peuple d’Israël. \q Maintenant, c’est Babylone elle-même qui doit tomber.

sw.L: Babeli nayo itaanguka, \q kwa ajili ya waliouawa wa Israeli, \q kama vile kwa ajili ya Babeli waliouawa wa dunia yote walivyoanguka.
sw.B: Babeli ni lazima ianguke \q kwa sababu ya waliouawa wa Israeli, \q kama vile kwa sababu ya Babeli waliouawa wa dunia yote walivyoanguka.
sw.R: Babeli iliwaua watu duniani kote. \q Iliwaua watu wa Israeli pia. \q Sasa Babeli yenyewe ni lazima ianguke.

decisions.choice: Babylon must fall for the slain of Israel: her fall pays for those she killed
alternatives: Babylon too must fall, O slain of Israel
decisions.reason: The two halves are joined by "also ... also", setting Babylon's fall beside the deaths she caused: as the nations' dead fell because of Babylon, so Babylon must fall because of Israel's dead. The words "slain of Israel" could also be a call to the dead, "Babylon too must fall, O slain of Israel", but the parallel with "for Babylon" favors "for the slain of Israel".

decisions.choice: the Greek lacks the first half of this verse
decisions.reason: As noted at verse 44, the Greek translation lacks the text from verse 44b to "the slain of Israel" here (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: Babylon killed people all over the world ... Now Babylon herself must fall
decisions.reason: Readable sets out the comparison in the order of events, so the reason for Babylon's fall comes first.

source.text: פְּלֵטִ֣ים מֵחֶ֔רֶב הִלְכ֖וּ אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹ֑דוּ זִכְר֤וּ מֵֽרָחוֹק֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה וִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֖ם תַּעֲלֶ֥ה עַל־לְבַבְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [O] escapees from [the] sword, go, do not stand; remember from afar Yahweh, and Jerusalem let it come up on your heart.

en.L: You who have escaped the sword, \q go, do not stand still! \q Remember {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from afar, \q and let Jerusalem come up into your heart.
en.B: You who have escaped the sword, \q go! Do not linger! \q Remember {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in that distant land, \q and let Jerusalem come to your mind.
en.R: You who did not die in the war, \q leave Babylon! Do not wait! \q You are far from home, but remember {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Think about Jerusalem.

es.L: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los que escaparon de la espada, \q ¡{{plural_you:váyanse|idos}}, no {{plural_you:se detengan|os detengáis}}! \q {{plural_you:Acuérdense|Acordaos}} desde lejos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q y que Jerusalén suba a {{plural_you:su corazón|vuestro corazón}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los que escaparon de la espada, \q ¡{{plural_you:váyanse|idos}}! ¡No {{plural_you:se queden|os quedéis}}! \q {{plural_you:Acuérdense|Acordaos}} {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} en esa tierra lejana, \q y que Jerusalén venga a {{plural_you:su mente|vuestra mente}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los que no murieron en la guerra, \q ¡{{plural_you:salgan|salid}} de Babilonia! ¡No {{plural_you:esperen|esperéis}}! \q {{plural_you:Están|Estáis}} lejos de casa, pero {{plural_you:acuérdense|acordaos}} {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. \q {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en Jerusalén.

fr.L: Vous qui avez échappé à l’épée, \q partez, ne vous arrêtez pas ! \q Souvenez-vous de loin {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q et que Jérusalem monte dans votre cœur.
fr.B: Vous qui avez échappé à l’épée, \q partez ! Ne vous attardez pas ! \q Dans ce pays lointain, souvenez-vous {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q et que Jérusalem vous revienne à l’esprit.
fr.R: Vous qui n’êtes pas morts à la guerre, \q quittez Babylone ! N’attendez pas ! \q Vous êtes loin de chez vous, mais souvenez-vous {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. \q Pensez à Jérusalem.

sw.L: Ninyi mliookoka upanga, \q nendeni, msisimame! \q Mkumbukeni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mkiwa mbali, \q na Yerusalemu iingie mioyoni mwenu.
sw.B: Ninyi mliookoka upanga, \q nendeni! Msikawie! \q Mkumbukeni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mkiwa katika nchi ile ya mbali, \q na Yerusalemu iwe akilini mwenu.
sw.R: Ninyi ambao hamkufa vitani, \q ondokeni Babeli! Msingoje! \q Mko mbali na nyumbani, lakini mkumbukeni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Ifikirieni Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: you who have escaped the sword: the exiles of Judah who survived
decisions.reason: The survivors are those of Judah who lived through the wars and were carried to Babylon (44:28). They are told to leave as Babylon falls (verses 6, 45).

decisions.choice: remember the LORD from afar; let Jerusalem come up into your heart
decisions.reason: "From afar" means from the far country of exile (30:10; Zechariah 10:9). To have something "come up on the heart" is to think of it and long for it (3:16; Psalm 137:5-6).

decisions.choice: come to your mind (B); Think about (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m2). Literal keeps "come up into your heart".

source.text: בֹּ֚שְׁנוּ כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֣עְנוּ חֶרְפָּ֔ה כִּסְּתָ֥ה כְלִמָּ֖ה פָּנֵ֑ינוּ כִּ֚י בָּ֣אוּ זָרִ֔ים עַֽל־מִקְדְּשֵׁ֖י בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: We are ashamed, for we have heard insult; has covered disgrace our faces, for have come strangers into [the] sanctuaries of [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: "We are ashamed, for we have heard insult; \q disgrace has covered our faces, \q for strangers have come \q into the sanctuaries of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house."
en.B: "We are ashamed, for we have heard insults; \q disgrace covers our faces, \q because foreigners have gone into \q the holy places of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house."
en.R: "We are ashamed, because people insult us. \q Our faces show our shame, \q because foreigners have gone \q into the holy places of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple."

es.L: «Estamos avergonzados, porque hemos oído la afrenta; \q la vergüenza ha cubierto nuestros rostros, \q porque han entrado extranjeros \q en los santuarios de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».
es.B: «Estamos avergonzados, porque hemos oído insultos; \q la vergüenza cubre nuestros rostros, \q porque los extranjeros han entrado \q en los lugares santos de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».
es.R: «Estamos avergonzados, porque la gente nos insulta. \q Nuestras caras muestran nuestra vergüenza, \q porque los extranjeros han entrado \q en los lugares santos del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».

fr.L: « Nous sommes honteux, car nous avons entendu l’insulte ; \q la confusion a couvert nos visages, \q car des étrangers sont venus \q dans les sanctuaires de la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »
fr.B: « Nous avons honte, car nous avons entendu des insultes ; \q la confusion couvre nos visages, \q parce que des étrangers sont entrés \q dans les lieux saints de la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »
fr.R: « Nous avons honte, parce qu’on nous insulte. \q Nos visages montrent notre honte, \q parce que des étrangers sont entrés \q dans les lieux saints du temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »

sw.L: "Tumeona haya, kwa maana tumesikia matukano; \q fedheha imefunika nyuso zetu, \q kwa maana wageni wameingia \q katika patakatifu pa nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.B: "Tumeaibika, kwa maana tumesikia matusi; \q fedheha imefunika nyuso zetu, \q kwa sababu wageni wameingia \q katika mahali patakatifu pa nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.R: "Tumeaibika, kwa sababu watu wanatutukana. \q Nyuso zetu zinaonyesha aibu yetu, \q kwa sababu wageni wameingia \q katika mahali patakatifu pa hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."

decisions.choice: we are ashamed: the exiles answer
decisions.reason: The exiles told to remember Jerusalem (verse 50) reply: they cannot think of it without shame, for the temple has been defiled. The LORD answers them in verse 52 with "Therefore".

decisions.choice: strangers have come into the sanctuaries: foreigners entered the holy places, which the law forbade
decisions.reason: Only priests could enter the holy rooms of the temple, and no foreigner could come into the sanctuary (Numbers 18:7; Ezekiel 44:7-9). The Babylonians went in, looted and burned it (52:13, 17-23; Lamentations 1:10; Psalm 79:1). "Sanctuaries" is plural, for the temple's holy rooms and courts.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for the exiles' words
decisions.reason: The exiles' reply is speech quoted inside the oracle, so it takes double quotation marks.

decisions.choice: « » for the exiles' words
decisions.reason: The exiles answer, and their words take quotation marks within the oracle.

source.text: לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה־יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וּפָקַדְתִּ֖י עַל־פְּסִילֶ֑יהָ וּבְכָל־אַרְצָ֖הּ יֶאֱנֹ֥ק חָלָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore here days coming, declares Yahweh, and I will punish her idols, and through all her land will groan [the] wounded.

en.L: Therefore, look, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q when I will punish her idols, \q and through all her land the wounded will groan.
en.B: Therefore the days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q when I will bring punishment on her idols, \q and the dying will groan in every part of her land.
en.R: So the time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q when I will punish Babylon's idols. \q All over her land, wounded people will groan.

es.L: Por tanto, he aquí vienen días, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q en que castigaré a sus ídolos, \q y en toda su tierra gemirán los heridos.
es.B: Por eso vienen días, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q en que castigaré a sus ídolos, \q y los moribundos gemirán en todo su territorio.
es.R: Por eso se acerca el tiempo, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q en que castigaré a los ídolos de Babilonia. \q Por toda su tierra gemirán los heridos.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, voici, des jours viennent, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q où je punirai ses idoles, \q et dans tout son pays les blessés gémiront.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi des jours viennent, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q où je punirai ses idoles, \q et les mourants gémiront dans tout son pays.
fr.R: C’est pourquoi un temps vient, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q où je punirai les idoles de Babylone. \q Partout dans son pays, les blessés gémiront.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo, tazama, siku zinakuja, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q nitakapoziadhibu sanamu zake, \q na katika nchi yake yote waliojeruhiwa wataugua.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo siku zinakuja, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q nitakapoleta adhabu juu ya sanamu zake, \q na wanaokufa wataugua katika kila sehemu ya nchi yake.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo wakati unakuja, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q nitakapoziadhibu sanamu za Babeli. \q Kila mahali katika nchi yake watu waliojeruhiwa wataugua.

decisions.choice: days are coming when I will punish her idols: as verse 47
decisions.reason: The words of verse 47 return as the LORD's answer to the exiles' shame: Babylon's gods, who seemed to have won over the LORD's house, will be judged.

decisions.choice: the wounded will groan: those fatally wounded moan as they die
decisions.reason: The word means one pierced and dying (verse 4; Ezekiel 26:15). Babylon's land will be filled with the groans of the dying, as Jerusalem was.

decisions.choice: as verse 47
decisions.reason: The formula keeps the wording of verse 47.

source.text: כִּֽי־תַעֲלֶ֤ה בָבֶל֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְכִ֥י תְבַצֵּ֖ר מְר֣וֹם עֻזָּ֑הּ מֵאִתִּ֗י יָבֹ֧אוּ שֹׁדְדִ֛ים לָ֖הּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Though should go up Babylon [to] the heavens, and though she should fortify [the] height of her strength, from me will come destroyers to her, declares Yahweh.

en.L: Though Babylon should go up to the heavens, \q and though she should fortify her strong height, \q from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} destroyers will come to her, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Even if Babylon should climb to the heavens \q and make her lofty stronghold secure, \q I will send destroyers against her, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Babylon may build her walls as high as the sky. \q She may make her high towers strong. \q But I will still send armies to destroy her, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Aunque Babilonia suba hasta los cielos, \q y aunque fortifique la altura de su fortaleza, \q de mi parte vendrán contra ella destructores, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Aunque Babilonia suba hasta los cielos \q y haga inexpugnable su alta fortaleza, \q yo enviaré destructores contra ella, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Babilonia puede construir sus muros tan altos como el cielo. \q Puede hacer fuertes sus altas torres. \q Pero aun así yo enviaré ejércitos a destruirla, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Même si Babylone montait jusqu’aux cieux, \q et même si elle fortifiait sa hauteur puissante, \q de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} part des dévastateurs viendront contre elle, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Même si Babylone montait jusqu’au ciel \q et rendait inaccessible sa haute forteresse, \q je lui enverrais des dévastateurs, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Babylone peut construire ses murailles aussi haut que le ciel. \q Elle peut rendre ses hautes tours solides. \q J’enverrai quand même des armées pour la détruire, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Ingawa Babeli angepanda mpaka mbinguni, \q na ingawa angeimarisha kimo cha nguvu zake, \q kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} waharibu watamjia, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Hata kama Babeli angepanda mpaka mbinguni \q na kuifanya ngome yake ya juu kuwa salama, \q nitawatuma waharibu dhidi yake, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Babeli anaweza kujenga kuta zake juu kama anga. \q Anaweza kuifanya minara yake mirefu kuwa imara. \q Lakini bado nitatuma majeshi kumwangamiza, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: go up to the heavens: Babylon's pride, like the tower of Babel
decisions.reason: The words recall the builders of Babel, who wanted a tower with its top in the heavens (Genesis 11:4), and the king of Babylon who said, "I will go up to the heavens" (Isaiah 14:13-14). No height can keep the LORD's destroyers out (49:16; Obadiah 4).

decisions.choice: from me: sent by the LORD
decisions.reason: The destroyers come "from with me", that is, at the LORD's command.

decisions.choice: I will send destroyers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "I will send" for "from me ... will come" (m2).

source.text: ק֥וֹל זְעָקָ֖ה מִבָּבֶ֑ל וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּד֖וֹל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sound of a cry from Babylon, and great destruction from [the] land of [the] Chaldeans!

en.L: The sound of a cry from Babylon, \q and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!
en.B: Listen! A cry rises from Babylon, \q the crash of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!
en.R: Listen! People in Babylon are crying out. \q There is a great crash of destruction in the land of Babylonia.

es.L: ¡Voz de clamor desde Babilonia, \q y gran destrucción desde la tierra de los caldeos!
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! Un grito se levanta desde Babilonia, \q el estruendo de una gran destrucción desde la tierra de los caldeos.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! La gente de Babilonia está gritando. \q Hay un gran estruendo de destrucción en la tierra de Babilonia.

fr.L: Le bruit d’un cri, de Babylone, \q et d’un grand désastre, du pays des Chaldéens !
fr.B: Écoutez ! Un cri monte de Babylone, \q le fracas d’un grand désastre au pays des Chaldéens !
fr.R: Écoutez ! Les gens de Babylone crient. \q On entend le grand fracas de la destruction au pays de Babylonie.

sw.L: Sauti ya kilio kutoka Babeli, \q na maangamizi makuu kutoka nchi ya Wakaldayo!
sw.B: Sikilizeni! Kilio kinapanda kutoka Babeli, \q mshindo wa maangamizi makuu kutoka nchi ya Wakaldayo!
sw.R: Sikilizeni! Watu wa Babeli wanalia. \q Kuna mshindo mkubwa wa maangamizi katika nchi ya Babeli.

decisions.choice: the sound of a cry ... great destruction: a cry of distress and the crash of ruin
decisions.reason: The first word can mean "sound" or serve as an exclamation, "Listen!" The cry is a scream for help; "destruction" is literally "breaking", a crash of ruin (4:6; 48:3, 5; 50:22, where nearly the same words are said of the land).

decisions.choice: Listen!
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the first word as an exclamation, which carries over to the second half (m1).

source.text: כִּֽי־שֹׁדֵ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־בָּבֶ֔ל וְאִבַּ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נָּה ק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל וְהָמ֤וּ גַלֵּיהֶם֙ כְּמַ֣יִם רַבִּ֔ים נִתַּ֥ן שְׁא֖וֹן קוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For [is] destroying Yahweh Babylon, and he will make perish from her [the] great voice; and roar their waves like many waters; is given [the] uproar of their voice.

en.L: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is destroying Babylon, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will silence her great voice; \q and their waves roar like many waters; \q the uproar of their voice resounds.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is destroying Babylon \q and silencing her loud noise. \q Their waves roar like mighty waters; \q the din of their voices rises.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is destroying Babylon. \q He will make her loud noise go silent. \q The enemy armies roar like great ocean waves. \q Their shouting grows louder and louder.

es.L: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} destruye a Babilonia, \q y hará callar su gran voz; \q y rugen sus olas como muchas aguas; \q resuena el estruendo de su voz.
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está destruyendo a Babilonia \q y acallando su gran bullicio. \q Sus olas rugen como aguas caudalosas; \q se levanta el estruendo de sus voces.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está destruyendo a Babilonia. \q Hará callar su gran ruido. \q Los ejércitos enemigos rugen como las grandes olas del mar. \q Sus gritos se oyen cada vez más fuertes.

fr.L: Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dévaste Babylone, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fera taire sa grande voix ; \q et leurs vagues grondent comme les grandes eaux ; \q le tumulte de leur voix retentit.
fr.B: Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dévaste Babylone \q et fait taire son grand vacarme. \q Leurs vagues grondent comme des eaux puissantes ; \q le tumulte de leurs voix s’élève.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} détruit Babylone. \q Il fera taire son grand vacarme. \q Les armées ennemies grondent comme les grandes vagues de l’océan. \q Leurs cris deviennent de plus en plus forts.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anaiharibu Babeli, \q naye atainyamazisha sauti yake kuu; \q nayo mawimbi yao yananguruma kama maji mengi; \q kelele ya sauti yao inavuma.
sw.B: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anaiangamiza Babeli \q na kuinyamazisha kelele yake kuu. \q Mawimbi yao yananguruma kama maji makuu; \q makelele ya sauti zao yanapanda.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anaiangamiza Babeli. \q Ataifanya kelele yake kuu inyamaze. \q Majeshi ya adui yananguruma kama mawimbi makubwa ya bahari. \q Kelele zao zinazidi kuwa kubwa.

decisions.choice: silence her great voice: put an end to the noise of the busy city
decisions.reason: The verb means to destroy or make perish, and with "voice" it means to silence. The "great voice" is the noise of a crowded city, its trade and its celebrations (7:34; 25:10).

decisions.choice: their waves roar like many waters: the attacking armies come like a raging sea
decisions.reason: "Their" most likely refers to the attackers, pictured again as a sea (verse 42; Isaiah 17:12-13). Babylon's noise is silenced, and the noise of the invaders takes its place.

decisions.choice: The enemy armies
decisions.reason: Readable names whose waves these are (m2).

source.text: כִּי֩ בָ֨א עָלֶ֤יהָ עַל־בָּבֶל֙ שׁוֹדֵ֔ד וְנִלְכְּדוּ֙ גִּבּוֹרֶ֔יהָ חִתְּתָ֖ה קַשְּׁתוֹתָ֑ם כִּ֣י אֵ֧ל גְּמֻל֛וֹת יְהוָ֖ה שַׁלֵּ֥ם יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For has come against her, against Babylon, a destroyer, and are captured her warriors; are shattered their bows; for a God of recompenses [is] Yahweh; repaying he will repay.

en.L: For a destroyer has come against her, against Babylon, \q and her warriors are captured, \q their bows are shattered, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] a God of recompense; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will surely repay.
en.B: For a destroyer has come against her, against Babylon. \q Her warriors are captured, \q their bows are broken, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is a God who repays; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will repay in full.
en.R: A destroyer has come to attack Babylon. \q Her soldiers are captured. \q Their bows are broken. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is a God who gives people what they deserve. He will pay Babylon back in full.

es.L: Porque viene contra ella, contra Babilonia, el destructor, \q y sus valientes son apresados, \q sus arcos quebrados, \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [es] Dios de retribuciones; ciertamente dará la paga.
es.B: Porque ha llegado el destructor contra ella, contra Babilonia. \q Sus guerreros son capturados, \q sus arcos están rotos, \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es un Dios que da a cada uno lo que merece; pagará por completo.
es.R: Un destructor ha llegado para atacar a Babilonia. \q Sus soldados son capturados. \q Sus arcos están rotos. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es un Dios que le da a cada uno lo que merece. Le dará a Babilonia su merecido por completo.

fr.L: Car le dévastateur est venu contre elle, contre Babylone, \q et ses guerriers sont pris, \q leurs arcs sont brisés, \q car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [est] un Dieu de rétribution ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rendra sûrement.
fr.B: Car le dévastateur est venu contre elle, contre Babylone. \q Ses guerriers sont capturés, \q leurs arcs sont brisés, \q car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est un Dieu qui rétribue ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rendra pleinement.
fr.R: Le dévastateur est venu attaquer Babylone. \q Ses soldats sont capturés. \q Leurs arcs sont brisés. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est un Dieu qui donne à chacun ce qu’il mérite. Il fera payer Babylone entièrement.

sw.L: Kwa maana mharibu amemjia, amejia Babeli, \q na mashujaa wake wamekamatwa, \q pinde zao zimevunjwavunjwa, \q kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ni] Mungu wa malipo; hakika atalipa.
sw.B: Kwa maana mharibu amemjia, amekuja juu ya Babeli. \q Mashujaa wake wamekamatwa, \q pinde zao zimevunjika, \q kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni Mungu anayelipa; atalipa kikamilifu.
sw.R: Mharibu amekuja kuishambulia Babeli. \q Askari wake wamekamatwa. \q Pinde zao zimevunjika. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni Mungu anayewapa watu wanachostahili. Ataulipiza Babeli kikamilifu.

decisions.choice: a God of recompense: the LORD gives each what their deeds deserve
decisions.reason: The plural noun is from the root of "recompense" in verse 6 and "repay" here. The LORD is a God who repays: he does not leave wrong unanswered (Deuteronomy 32:35, 41; Isaiah 59:18). The doubled verb, "repaying he will repay", makes the promise certain and complete.

decisions.choice: their bows are shattered: the army's weapons broken
decisions.reason: The bow stands for a nation's military strength (49:35; Hosea 1:5). The archers of verse 3 now lose their bows.

decisions.choice: will surely repay (L); will repay in full (B, R)
decisions.reason: Each level renders the doubled verb (m1) with a word of emphasis.

source.text: וְ֠הִשְׁכַּרְתִּי שָׂרֶ֨יהָ וַחֲכָמֶ֜יהָ פַּחוֹתֶ֤יהָ וּסְגָנֶ֨יהָ֙ וְגִבּוֹרֶ֔יהָ וְיָשְׁנ֥וּ שְׁנַת־עוֹלָ֖ם וְלֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ נְאֻ֨ם־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will make drunk her princes and her wise men, her governors and her officials and her warriors, and they will sleep a sleep of forever and not wake, declares the King, Yahweh of hosts [is] his name.

en.L: And I will make drunk her princes and her wise men, her governors and her officials and her warriors, \q and they will sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake, \q declares the King, \q whose name [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: I will make her officials and wise men drunk, her governors, deputies and warriors, \q and they will sleep a sleep that lasts forever and never wake, \q declares the King, \q whose name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: I will make her leaders and wise men drunk, and her governors, officials and soldiers. \q Then they will fall asleep forever and never wake up, \q says the King, \q whose name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

es.L: Y embriagaré a sus príncipes y a sus sabios, a sus gobernadores, a sus magistrados y a sus valientes, \q y dormirán un sueño perpetuo y no despertarán, \q declara el Rey, \q cuyo nombre [es] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos.
es.B: Emborracharé a sus jefes y a sus sabios, a sus gobernadores, a sus delegados y a sus guerreros, \q y dormirán un sueño que dure para siempre y nunca despertarán, \q afirma el Rey, \q cuyo nombre es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: Emborracharé a sus dirigentes y a sus sabios, a sus gobernadores, a sus funcionarios y a sus soldados. \q Luego se dormirán para siempre y nunca despertarán, \q dice el Rey, \q cuyo nombre es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

fr.L: Et j’enivrerai ses princes et ses sages, ses gouverneurs et ses magistrats et ses guerriers, \q et ils dormiront d’un sommeil éternel et ne se réveilleront pas, \q déclare le Roi, \q dont le nom [est] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: J’enivrerai ses chefs et ses sages, ses gouverneurs, ses magistrats et ses guerriers, \q et ils dormiront d’un sommeil sans fin et ne se réveilleront jamais, \q déclare le Roi, \q dont le nom est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: J’enivrerai ses chefs et ses sages, ses gouverneurs, ses magistrats et ses soldats. \q Puis ils s’endormiront pour toujours et ne se réveilleront jamais, \q dit le Roi, \q dont le nom est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.

sw.L: Nami nitawalevya wakuu wake na wenye hekima wake, maliwali wake na maafisa wake na mashujaa wake, \q nao watalala usingizi wa milele wasiamke, \q asema Mfalme, \q ambaye jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.B: Nitawalevya maafisa wake na wenye hekima wake, maliwali wake, manaibu wake na mashujaa wake, \q nao watalala usingizi wa milele wasiamke kamwe, \q asema Mfalme, \q ambaye jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.R: Nitawalevya viongozi wake na wenye hekima wake, maliwali wake, maafisa wake na askari wake. \q Kisha watalala usingizi milele wala hawataamka kamwe, \q anasema Mfalme, \q ambaye jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.

decisions.choice: make drunk ... sleep a perpetual sleep: the words of verse 39 return
decisions.reason: The feast of verse 39 is now given to Babylon's leaders. All the ranks of her rulers drink the LORD's cup and die. The words are those of verse 39.

decisions.choice: the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts: the true king above the king of Babylon
decisions.reason: The title answers the "king of Babylon" (verses 31, 34). The LORD is the King of all the earth (10:7, 10; 46:18; 48:15).

decisions.choice: princes, governors, officials: the ranks of the empire's rulers
decisions.reason: As in verse 23, governors and officials are titles of the empire's provincial rulers; princes are the court's leading men.

decisions.choice: princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R); her officials (L), deputies (B), officials (R)
decisions.reason: *Sar* follows the settled wording: "princes", "officials", "leaders". Since Balanced already uses "officials" for *sar*, it says "deputies" for the second title, which is "officials" in verse 23. The words about sleep keep the wording of verse 39 at each level.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת חֹ֠מוֹת בָּבֶ֤ל הָֽרְחָבָה֙ עַרְעֵ֣ר תִּתְעַרְעָ֔ר וּשְׁעָרֶ֥יהָ הַגְּבֹהִ֖ים בָּאֵ֣שׁ יִצַּ֑תּוּ וְיִֽגְע֨וּ עַמִּ֧ים בְּדֵי־רִ֛יק וּלְאֻמִּ֥ים בְּדֵי־אֵ֖שׁ וְיָעֵֽפוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts: [The] walls of Babylon, the broad, utterly will be laid bare, and her gates, the high, with fire will be burned; and toil peoples for nothing, and nations for fire, and they grow weary.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: The broad wall of Babylon will be utterly laid bare, \q and her high gates will be burned with fire; \q and peoples toil for nothing, and nations for fire, and they grow weary.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: The broad wall of Babylon will be leveled to the ground, \q and her high gates will be set on fire. \q The peoples toil for nothing; the nations wear themselves out only for the fire.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Babylon's thick walls will be completely torn down. \q Her tall gates will be burned. \q The people of the nations worked hard to build them, but it was all for nothing. They wore themselves out, only for it all to burn.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: El ancho muro de Babilonia será derribado por completo, \q y sus altas puertas serán quemadas con fuego; \q y los pueblos trabajan para nada, y las naciones para el fuego, y se cansan.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: El ancho muro de Babilonia será arrasado hasta el suelo, \q y sus altas puertas serán incendiadas. \q Los pueblos se fatigan para nada; las naciones se agotan solo para el fuego.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: Las gruesas murallas de Babilonia serán derribadas por completo. \q Sus altas puertas serán quemadas. \q La gente de las naciones trabajó mucho para construirlas, pero todo fue en vano. Se agotaron para que todo terminara quemado.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : La large muraille de Babylone sera entièrement rasée, \q et ses hautes portes seront brûlées par le feu ; \q et les peuples se fatiguent pour le néant, et les nations pour le feu, et ils s’épuisent.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : La large muraille de Babylone sera rasée jusqu’au sol, \q et ses hautes portes seront livrées au feu. \q Les peuples se fatiguent pour rien ; les nations s’épuisent seulement pour le feu.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Les épaisses murailles de Babylone seront complètement démolies. \q Ses hautes portes seront brûlées. \q Les gens des nations ont travaillé dur pour les construire, mais tout cela n’a servi à rien. Ils se sont épuisés, et tout va brûler.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Ukuta mpana wa Babeli utabomolewa kabisa, \q na malango yake marefu yatateketezwa kwa moto; \q na mataifa wanajitaabisha bure, na mataifa kwa ajili ya moto, nao wanachoka.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Ukuta mpana wa Babeli utabomolewa mpaka chini, \q na malango yake marefu yatachomwa moto. \q Mataifa wanajitaabisha bure; mataifa wanajichosha kwa ajili ya moto tu.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Kuta nene za Babeli zitabomolewa kabisa. \q Malango yake marefu yatachomwa moto. \q Watu wa mataifa walifanya kazi kwa bidii kuyajenga, lakini yote yalikuwa bure. Walijichosha, ili tu yote yaungue.

decisions.choice: the broad wall ... utterly laid bare: Babylon's great walls razed to their foundations
decisions.reason: The noun is plural, "walls", for the whole system of walls, with a singular adjective "broad". Babylon's double walls were famous for their width. The doubled verb means to strip to the ground, to raze completely.

decisions.choice: peoples toil for nothing, nations for fire: the same saying as Habakkuk 2:13
decisions.reason: Habakkuk 2:13 has almost the same words in the reverse order: "peoples toil for fire, and nations weary themselves for nothing". It is a saying about empires built by forced labor: all their work ends in flames. Habakkuk has not yet been translated in this project; when it is, the two should be compared. The last verb, "and they grow weary", returns at the end of verse 64.

decisions.choice: for nothing: for the sake of emptiness
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "for enough of emptiness", that is, their labor gains them nothing but emptiness, and "enough of fire", only enough to feed the flames.

decisions.choice: utterly laid bare (L); leveled to the ground (B); completely torn down (R); wear themselves out only for the fire (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the doubled verb means (m1) and make the last line clear. Readable adds that the peoples built the walls, which the saying implies.

decisions.choice: y se cansan (L)
decisions.reason: The last words, "and they will grow weary", return in verse 64; they echo Habakkuk 2:13.

source.text: הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֣ה׀יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֗יא אֶת־שְׂרָיָ֣ה בֶן־נֵרִיָּה֮ בֶּן־מַחְסֵיָה֒ בְּלֶכְתּ֞וֹ אֶת־צִדְקִיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ בָּבֶ֔ל בִּשְׁנַ֥ת הָרְבִעִ֖ית לְמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׂרָיָ֖ה שַׂ֥ר מְנוּחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: The word that commanded Jeremiah the prophet Seraiah son of Neriah son of Mahseiah in his going with Zedekiah king of Judah [to] Babylon in the fourth year of his reigning; and Seraiah [was] officer of [the] resting place.

en.L: The word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Now Seraiah [was] officer of the resting place.
en.B: This is the message that Jeremiah the prophet gave as a command to Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was the quartermaster.
en.R: This is the message that Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah son of Neriah and grandson of Mahseiah. Seraiah was going to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah. This was in Zedekiah's fourth year as king. Seraiah was the officer in charge of the places where the king stopped to rest on the journey.

es.L: La palabra que Jeremías el profeta mandó a Seraías hijo de Nerías, hijo de Maasías, cuando fue con Sedequías, rey de Judá, a Babilonia en el año cuarto de su reinado. Y Seraías [era] jefe del lugar de descanso.
es.B: Este es el mensaje que el profeta Jeremías le dio como orden a Seraías hijo de Nerías, hijo de Maasías, cuando fue a Babilonia con Sedequías, rey de Judá, en el cuarto año de su reinado. Seraías era el jefe de alojamiento.
es.R: Este es el mensaje que el profeta Jeremías le dio a Seraías, hijo de Nerías y nieto de Maasías. Seraías iba a Babilonia con Sedequías, rey de Judá. Era el cuarto año del reinado de Sedequías. Seraías era el oficial encargado de los lugares donde el rey se detenía a descansar durante el viaje.

fr.L: La parole que Jérémie le prophète commanda à Seraya fils de Nériya, fils de Mahséya, quand il alla avec Sédécias, roi de Juda, à Babylone, en la quatrième année de son règne. Or Seraya [était] chef des étapes.
fr.B: Voici l’ordre que le prophète Jérémie donna à Seraya fils de Nériya, fils de Mahséya, quand celui-ci se rendit à Babylone avec Sédécias, roi de Juda, la quatrième année de son règne. Seraya était le responsable des étapes.
fr.R: Voici le message que le prophète Jérémie a donné à Seraya, fils de Nériya et petit-fils de Mahséya. Seraya partait pour Babylone avec Sédécias, roi de Juda. C’était la quatrième année du règne de Sédécias. Seraya était l’officier chargé des endroits où le roi s’arrêtait pour se reposer pendant le voyage.

sw.L: Neno ambalo Yeremia nabii alimwagiza Seraya mwana wa Neria, mwana wa Maseya, alipokwenda pamoja na Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda hata Babeli katika mwaka wa nne wa kutawala kwake. Naye Seraya [alikuwa] afisa wa mahali pa kupumzika.
sw.B: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao nabii Yeremia alimpa kama agizo Seraya mwana wa Neria, mwana wa Maseya, alipokwenda Babeli pamoja na Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda katika mwaka wa nne wa utawala wake. Seraya alikuwa msimamizi wa makao ya safari.
sw.R: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao nabii Yeremia alimpa Seraya mwana wa Neria na mjukuu wa Maseya. Seraya alikuwa akienda Babeli pamoja na Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda. Hii ilikuwa katika mwaka wa nne wa utawala wa Sedekia. Seraya alikuwa afisa aliyesimamia mahali ambapo mfalme alisimama kupumzika safarini.

decisions.choice: Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah: the brother of Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe
decisions.reason: Baruch is "son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah" (32:12; 36:4), so Seraiah, with the same father and grandfather, was his brother. One brother wrote down Jeremiah's words in Jerusalem; the other carried his word against Babylon to Babylon itself.

decisions.choice: with Zedekiah ... in the fourth year of his reign: about 594 BC
decisions.reason: Zedekiah's fourth year is the year of chapters 27-28, when envoys of other kings met in Jerusalem to plan revolt against Babylon. A journey to Babylon that year may have been to assure Nebuchadrezzar of Judah's loyalty. The trip is not mentioned elsewhere. The Greek translation reads "from Zedekiah", making Seraiah the king's envoy rather than his companion (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: officer of the resting place: probably the quartermaster, in charge of the stops on the journey
alternatives: officer in charge of the tribute
decisions.reason: The title means "officer of the resting place" and is found only here. It most likely names the official who arranged where the king's party would halt and lodge on the way. Its exact meaning is uncertain. The Greek translation reads "officer of gifts", from Hebrew letters close to those of "tribute" (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: the word that Jeremiah commanded: a closing story in prose
decisions.reason: After the long poem against Babylon (50:1-51:58), the book tells how Jeremiah sent it to Babylon. These verses are prose narrative.

decisions.choice: quartermaster (B); the officer in charge of the places where the king stopped to rest (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the familiar title for the officer who arranged lodging on a march; Readable explains it. Literal keeps the Hebrew words. Readable says "grandson of Mahseiah", as in 32:12.

decisions.choice: jefe del lugar de descanso (L); jefe de alojamiento (B); el oficial encargado de los lugares donde el rey se detenía a descansar (R)
decisions.reason: The officer who arranged the stops on the king's journey; Seraías is the brother of Baruc son of Nerías (32:12).

decisions.choice: "afisa wa mahali pa kupumzika" (L); "msimamizi wa makao ya safari" (B); Readable spells it out
decisions.reason: As the English: the office is named literally at Literal and described at Balanced and Readable. This Seraiah, Baruch's brother, is not the chief priest of 52:24.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and passé composé (R) for verses 59-64
decisions.reason: The book closes with a short narrative; it follows the tenses set for narrative in French Jeremiah.

source.text: וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ אֵ֧ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־תָּב֥וֹא אֶל־בָּבֶ֖ל אֶל־סֵ֣פֶר אֶחָ֑ד אֵ֚ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה הַכְּתֻבִ֖ים אֶל־בָּבֶֽל׃

decisions.choice: all these words written concerning Babylon: the oracle of chapters 50-51
decisions.reason: The words most likely mean the poem just given (50:1-51:58), or the heart of it. The scroll is "one" because it was written for this single purpose, to be read and sunk in Babylon.

decisions.choice: wrote: had written, before Seraiah set out
decisions.reason: The verb tells what Jeremiah did to prepare for Seraiah's journey; the order of events allows "had written".

decisions.choice: written above
decisions.reason: Readable says "above" to make clear that the words are those of the preceding chapters (m1).

decisions.choice: and you will see, and you will read: see to it that you read
decisions.reason: The two verbs together mean "take care to read" (compare Exodus 25:40). It may also mean "look around you and read": read where the city can be seen.

decisions.choice: read aloud: proclaim the words in Babylon itself
decisions.reason: The verb means to read aloud. Whether many heard it or Seraiah read it for God alone, the word against Babylon was spoken in Babylon, as a prophetic act (verse 63).

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes in verse 64
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's instructions run to the end of verse 64; the words Seraiah is to say take single quotation marks. Readable ends the sentence here.

records.literal_gloss: and you will say: Yahweh, you have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, so that not [is] in it an inhabitant, from man to beast, for desolations of forever it will be.

en.L: and say, '{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, so that there will be no one dwelling in it, from human to animal, for it will be a desolation forever.'
en.B: and say, '{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have said that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will destroy this place, so that nothing will live in it, neither people nor animals, and it will be a desolation forever.'
en.R: Then say, '{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have said that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will destroy this place. No people or animals will live here. It will be an empty ruin forever.'

es.B: y di: “{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has dicho que destruirás este lugar, de modo que nada viva en él, ni personas ni animales, y que será una desolación para siempre”.
es.R: Luego di: “{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has dicho que destruirás este lugar. Ni personas ni animales vivirán aquí. Será una ruina vacía para siempre”.

fr.R: Puis dis : “{{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as dit que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} détruirais ce lieu. Ni les gens ni les animaux n’y vivront. Ce sera une ruine vide pour toujours.”

sw.B: na kusema, 'Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umesema kwamba utapaangamiza mahali hapa, hata kisiwepo kitu chochote kinachoishi ndani yake, wala watu wala wanyama, napo patakuwa ukiwa milele.'

decisions.choice: to cut it off ... from human to animal ... a desolation forever: the words of the oracle
decisions.reason: Seraiah repeats the oracle's own sentence: no one living there, human or animal (50:3; 51:29, 43), and a desolation forever (51:26). He holds God to his word in the place it concerns.

decisions.choice: LORD, you have spoken: Seraiah speaks to God
decisions.reason: The words are a prayer addressed to the LORD, not a message to the Babylonians.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for Seraiah's words
decisions.reason: What Seraiah is to say is quoted inside Jeremiah's speech, so it takes single quotation marks. The LORD is addressed without "O", as in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} (vocative, no article)
decisions.reason: YHWH addressed directly, as set in the terms note.

decisions.choice: "Ee BWANA" for the vocative
decisions.reason: The vocative form set in the Swahili Psalms (19:15); the free "wewe" for God takes the deity span.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}" in the vocative, without article
decisions.reason: The vocative as the French terms note sets it.

decisions.choice: tie a stone to it and throw it: an acted sign of Babylon's fall
decisions.reason: Like the loincloth of 13:1-11 and the broken jar of 19:1-13, the act shows what the words say: as the scroll sinks, so will Babylon (verse 64). Revelation 18:21 takes up the sign: an angel throws a great millstone into the sea and says Babylon will be thrown down like it.

decisions.choice: the Euphrates: the river of Babylon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the river, Perath, the Euphrates, which ran through the city of Babylon (13:4; 46:2).

decisions.choice: the Euphrates at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the river's name here, not "the River", so every level says "the Euphrates"; Readable adds "River".

decisions.choice: and they will grow weary: probably a phrase repeated by mistake from verse 58
alternatives: part of what Seraiah is to say
decisions.reason: The words end verse 58, where they make sense: the nations wear themselves out for nothing. Here they do not fit the sentence. They may have been copied as a marker of where the poem ended, before the story of verses 59-64 was placed after it, and then left in the text. The Greek translation lacks them (this is from general knowledge). They are kept here because they are in the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: I am bringing: the LORD's own words, spoken by Seraiah
decisions.reason: Seraiah's words turn into the LORD's own word, as the prophet's message does elsewhere: the "I" is the LORD.

decisions.choice: thus far the words of Jeremiah: the end of the book's collection of his words
decisions.reason: The note marks the end of Jeremiah's words. Chapter 52 is an appendix from the history of the kings, nearly the same as 2 Kings 24:18-25:30, telling of Jerusalem's fall and of King Jehoiachin's release in Babylon. It shows that Jeremiah's word came true. The Greek translation lacks this note (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: and they will grow weary kept inside Seraiah's words; the quotation closes
decisions.reason: The phrase stands where the Hebrew has it (m1), at the end of the quoted words. Readable sets it as a sentence of its own. Jeremiah's speech, opened in verse 61, closes here, before the closing note.

decisions.choice: y se cansarán, inside Seraiah's words
decisions.reason: The phrase from the end of verse 58 is kept inside the quoted words, before the note that Jeremiah's words end here (chapter 52 is an appendix).
